security_audit.summary: Most external command alerts are false positives caused by Markdown inline code or fenced command examples, not executable Ruby backticks. The hardcoded GitHub clone URL is a real low-severity network and supply-chain dependency, and the install flow should be reviewed before use.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded external repository in install instructions
remediation.suggestion: Document why this repository is trusted, pin a tag or commit, and align the install source with the marketplace source when possible.

remediation.issue: Manual commands run a separately cloned local agent manager
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to inspect the cloned scripts before running them and require confirmation before any automation starts or assigns agents.

content.value_statement: Coordinating many local CLI agents is hard when each needs a session, logs, and task handoff. This skill guides tmux-based agent management, monitoring, assignment, and recurring work.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use separate tmux sessions for local CLI agents.
Lists prerequisites for installing the agent manager and requiring tmux and python3.
Shows commands to check health, list agents, start agents, monitor logs, and assign tasks.
Describes that agent configuration belongs under an agents directory.
Sets boundaries for validation, permissions, and missing requirements.
limitations: The skill package does not include the agent-manager script source.
It requires tmux, python3, and a separately cloned repository.
Examples assume local shell access and existing agent definitions.
It does not replace environment-specific testing or safety review.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Parallel Maintenance Agents
use_cases.description: Run several local agents in separate tmux sessions while tracking status and output.

use_cases.title: Monitor Long-Running Agent Work
use_cases.description: Follow an agent session log while it handles a local task or workflow.

use_cases.title: Schedule Recurring Agent Tasks
use_cases.description: Use cron-friendly guidance to plan repeated local agent work with clear safety boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Check Agent Manager Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agent-manager skill to help me verify prerequisites and run a basic health check for local agents.

prompt_templates.title: Start and List Agents
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agent-manager skill to guide me through listing available agents and starting one named EMP_0001.

prompt_templates.title: Assign a Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agent-manager skill to assign a documented workflow to EMP_0002 and explain how I should monitor the result.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Recurring Agent Routine
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agent-manager skill to plan a cron-friendly routine for multiple agents, including validation steps and stop conditions.

output_examples.input: Help me check whether the agent manager is ready.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms tmux and python3 are required, then suggests a health check and agent listing before starting any session.

output_examples.input: I need EMP_0002 to follow a maintenance workflow.
output_examples.output: The assistant prepares an assignment flow, names the target agent, references the workflow file, and recommends monitoring the session output.
The assistant outlines a scheduled routine with prerequisites, agent selection, monitoring, validation, and clear stop conditions.

best_practices: Inspect the cloned agent manager repository before running local scripts.
Start with health checks and agent listing before assigning work.
Define permissions, success criteria, and stop conditions before scheduling recurring tasks.
anti_patterns: Do not run cloned scripts before reviewing the source and repository trust.
Do not assign broad tasks without clear safety boundaries.
Do not treat agent output as a substitute for testing or expert review.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It guides management of multiple local CLI agents through tmux sessions, monitoring, task assignment, and scheduling.

faq.question: Does it include the agent manager code?
faq.answer: No. The skill points users to clone a separate repository for the agent manager scripts.

faq.question: Which tools are required?
faq.answer: The documented prerequisites are tmux and python3.

faq.question: Can it start more than one agent?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes running multiple local CLI agents in separate tmux sessions.

faq.question: Can it assign tasks to an agent?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show assigning a workflow to a named agent and monitoring output.

faq.question: Is this safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: Review the external repository first, then use explicit permissions, validation, and stop conditions before automation.
